rubrics.criterion: The sign-up flow no longer inspects individual fields of the fetched account row (such as the stored email or stored password) when deciding whether an address is already registered; the account-existence decision is delegated to an operation owned by the persistence side (or equivalent single clean decision) instead of being re-derived in the page module.
rubrics.rationale: The registration screen's local helper re-validating fetched rows field by field is the sign-up manifestation of this case's record dissection; the existence rule belongs with the code that owns the account record.

rubrics.criterion: The credentials sign-in path no longer branches on the stored record's own fields before comparing the password; the decision that submitted credentials match a stored account (row lookup plus comparison against the stored hash) is made by the persistence-side code that defines and queries the record, not re-proved inside the NextAuth provider wiring.
rubrics.rationale: The authorize callback's row-completeness gate is the authentication manifestation of this case; the task prompt explicitly requires the stored-credential decision to move behind the data-access layer.

rubrics.criterion: The protected dashboard no longer derives its greeting by walking the stored account's identity fields (email, numeric id) through presentation-module logic; the rendered identity comes from the session value directly or from a single owner-provided identity, with the field-stepping derivation removed.
rubrics.rationale: The dashboard's local identity-derivation helper is the logged-in-display manifestation of this case; how an account is named is record knowledge, not presentation knowledge.

rubrics.criterion: Every flow touched by the relocation was rewired coherently: imports and call sites of the sign-up action, the credentials authorize callback, and the protected view reference the operations or data they now consume, with no dangling references to removed helpers and no module left importing something it no longer uses.
rubrics.rationale: Moving record decisions behind the persistence side changes three caller sites at once in this case; an incomplete rewiring leaves broken or half-updated consumers even if the moved code itself is correct.

rubrics.criterion: The relocated account-record decisions live in (or are exported by) the module that declares the account record mapping and performs its queries and inserts, reusing that module's existing record interfaces rather than introducing a parallel data source or raw queries elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: The case's ownership boundary is defined by the single pgTable('User', {...}) declaration; the repair is only complete when record rules share the record's home and lifecycle instead of spawning a second owner.

rubrics.criterion: The middleware-shared auth configuration remains free of new imports of the Node-only persistence module, so route-protection decisions still load in the Edge middleware runtime.
rubrics.rationale: This repository deliberately splits Node-only auth wiring from the Edge-compatible config; a relocation that drags database imports into the shared config breaks middleware loading even when surface behavior looks unchanged.

rubrics.criterion: The page-module and provider-wiring helpers that were inspecting account-record fields are removed outright once their job moves, rather than left in place unused (dead code), and no unused imports of theirs remain.
rubrics.rationale: The reorganization makes the local row-inspection scaffolding obsolete; leaving it behind as dead code is the specific incomplete-cleanup failure mode this case can produce.

rubrics.criterion: No live duplicate of the removed record-dissection logic reappears elsewhere: the same field-by-field checks are not inlined again at another call site or reintroduced as a differently named helper in flow code.
rubrics.rationale: A relocation that copies the dissection into a new shape rather than consolidating it with the record's owner would recreate this case's problem under a different name.

rubrics.criterion: Sign-up behavior is preserved end to end: an already-registered address still yields the 'User already exists' outcome (no duplicate row is inserted, and the table has no unique constraint to catch it), while a fresh address still creates the account and redirects to the login page.
rubrics.rationale: The existence decision is load-bearing: this case's greatest silent-failure risk is a sign-up repair that inserts duplicate accounts instead of reporting the duplicate.

rubrics.criterion: Credential sign-in behavior is preserved: a correct password authenticates and yields the matched account as the session user, a wrong password does not authenticate, and an unknown email yields no session.
rubrics.rationale: The authorize path is the app's only authentication mechanism; a relocation that loses the matched-account return or flips the comparison outcome breaks login silently.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not achieve the boundary by deleting required account behavior: removing the duplicate-address check entirely, skipping or stubbing the stored-hash comparison, or blanking/hardcoding the dashboard identity all fail this rubric even if all record reads are gone.
rubrics.rationale: The strongest temptation when draining record logic out of flow code is to drop the rule with it; this negative item pins the case's behavior as non-negotiable.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not weaken the account rules while moving them: no plaintext or constant comparison of the submitted password against a stored field, no change to the bcrypt hashing or comparison parameters, and no duplication of the existence/verification logic across multiple call sites.
rubrics.rationale: This case stores salted hashes at insert time; a careless consolidation could compare the raw input to the stored hash string or split the rule into copies that drift, which the prompt's preservation boundary forbids.
